dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt system (JMA standard receipt software), running on Linux with GnuCOBOL. Program ORCS02 is a patient co-payment calculation subprogram for inpatient use.
evidence: COPY count 38, CALL count 92 typical of ORCA suite
fixed format, no COMP-3 consistent with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL ORCA codebase

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance co-payment calculation for inpatient billing (JMA ORCA receipt system). Handles patient burden amount computation covering various insurance types, regional public expense subsidies, elderly patient rules, income-based limits, and meal/living expense charges.
purpose.summary: ORCS02 is a subprogram within the JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt software suite. It calculates patient co-payment (負担金算定) amounts for inpatient claims, handling a wide variety of Japanese health insurance rules including elderly patient thresholds, regional public expense subsidies, low-income exemptions, and meal/living expense charges. The extensive revision history (2002–2009) reflects ongoing adaptation to Japanese medical insurance law changes.

notable_features: Extensive Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1)
Very large single file: 28,257 lines, ~1.4 MB
92 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprogram architecture
685 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — batch subprogram
No COMP-3 usage (unusual for financial calculations, may use DISPLAY numerics)
Detailed revision history spanning 2002–2009 with 100+ named patches
verdict.notes: File is encoded in EUC-JP (Japanese) but decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in comment text. The COBOL structure and English portions are fully legible. This is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system. Source is truncated at 16000 chars but the structure is unambiguous from the header and mechanical indicators.
